Retaining Wall Installation Brisbane Homeowners Trust, and Fencing to Match Most enquiries start the same way: a block that falls away at the back, an old timber sleeper wall leaning a little further every wet season, and a boundary fence that has to sit on whatever gets built. That is why this site covers both trades rather than one. On the retaining side that means timber sleeper, concrete sleeper and core-filled besser block, which is hollow masonry with steel bars grouted into the cores, plus repair and replacement of walls that have aged out. On the fencing side it means Colorbond steel, lapped-and-capped timber palings, compliant pool barriers and driveway gates. Quoting the two together matters. A fence sitting on a retaining wall is assessed on the combined height, and a wall holding up a driveway or pool is carrying a surcharge load, which is weight pressing down behind the wall face, and that changes the engineering. Retaining walls Concrete Sleeper Retaining Walls Long-life reinforced concrete panels between galvanised posts, engineered for taller Brisbane and hinterland cuts. Timber Sleeper Retaining Walls H4 treated-pine terraces for garden edges and lower cuts, the common entry-point retaining wall build. Besser Block (Core-Filled) Retaining Walls Steel-reinforced core-filled block for taller structural retaining where timber and segmental block fall short. Retaining Wall Repairs & Replacement Assessing leaning, bulging or rotted walls on the 30-60 year old cuts common across established suburbs. Fencing and gates Colorbond Fencing Low-maintenance steel panel boundary lines in standard AU colours, from new-estate blocks to coastal renewals. Timber Fencing Lapped-and-capped paling fences for privacy lines on established Brisbane and hinterland streets. Pool Fencing Compliant glass and aluminium barriers built to the QLD pool safety standard, inspector sign-off ready. Gates & Gate Automation Sliding, swing and solar-automated driveway gates matched to the fence line and site access. Get your wall or fence properly quoted The single most common worry we hear is not whether the job will be expensive. It is whether the quote in front of you is fair. Tell us the height, the length, what is above the wall and how a truck gets in, and you will get a written quote you can actually compare, with excavation, drainage and backfill itemised rather than buried. Both trades handled in one conversation, not two. Approval and engineering triggers checked against your site, not a generic rule. Drainage treated as structural, because that is what fails walls.
